nodes.label: Prefer Native Elements over ARIA (SC 4.1.2)
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: Native interactive elements handle Enter/Space activation, focus and assistive-tech semantics for free, so manual keyboard handling is added only when a native element is impossible. ARIA roles and states are used only when native semantics do not exist.

nodes.label: Evidence-Led Accessibility Audit Workflow
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: Automated tools detect only a subset of accessibility barriers, so a score of 100 is not WCAG conformance and a low score does not replace issue-level evidence. Failed audit nodes are used to localize the offending component instead of searching the whole repository, and the same audit is re-run after the fix.

nodes.label: Agentic Browsing and AI Discoverability
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: Lighthouse Agentic Browsing measures technical signals that help an assistant read and interact with a rendered page (accessibility tree, optional llms.txt, WebMCP registrations). It is deliberately kept separate from search indexing/ranking and from AI ingestion/citation, because a browsable page or a valid llms.txt does not prove any AI product will ingest, rank or cite the content.

nodes.label: Product-Specific Crawler Controls
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: Crawler controls are audited per documented user agent instead of a blanket AI-bot rule, because training controls (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) are distinct from search and user-fetch controls (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User) and Google-Extended affects Gemini training/grounding rather than Google Search inclusion or ranking.

nodes.label: llms.txt (Optional)
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: llms.txt is an experimental proposal, not a cross-vendor discovery standard. It is added only on request or when a documented consumer supports it, and must never be treated as a ranking or citation factor, duplicated from the sitemap, or used to reorganize content solely to raise the audit.

nodes.label: Tap Targets
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: Mobile links need at least 48x48px hit areas and readable 16px font sizes so users can interact and read without zooming.

nodes.label: Structured Data (JSON-LD)
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: Schema markup must describe visible, accurate content using the most specific applicable type; a type or claim should never be added solely to obtain a rich result, and passing syntax validation does not guarantee search-engine eligibility or display.

nodes.label: Evidence-Led Audit Workflow
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: A Lighthouse SEO score covers only a useful subset of technical checks and is not a prediction of rankings. The workflow therefore separates technical crawl/index findings from content quality and authority, forbids inventing ranking-factor weights, and requires re-running the same checks after fixing the source, reporting indexation outcomes as still pending search-engine validation.

nodes.label: Canonical URLs
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: A self-referencing canonical is recommended so duplicate content issues are prevented, and canonical consistency across page templates is one of the signals Lighthouse cannot establish on its own.

nodes.label: Crawlability
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: robots.txt must not block resources the crawler needs in order to render the page (e.g. Disallow: /static/ blocks rendering assets), so crawl directives must be audited against the page's own resource needs.

nodes.label: XML Sitemap
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: A single sitemap is capped at 50,000 URLs or 50MB, so larger sites need a sitemap index; only canonical, indexable URLs belong in the sitemap and lastmod must be updated when content changes.

nodes.label: Heading Structure
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: The primary page heading must be descriptive and the hierarchy unambiguous, but a page should not fail solely because valid HTML contains more than one h1.

nodes.label: Meta Descriptions
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: The 150-160 character range is only a linting proxy because snippets are query- and device-dependent and Google may select page content instead of the meta description.

nodes.label: Title Tags
nodes.author: web-quality-skills
nodes.rationale: The 50-60 character rule is only a rough linting proxy, not a pass/fail limit: Google truncates title links to fit the rendered device width and may build a different title link from the visible title, headings and anchor text, so title-link rewriting must be treated separately from truncation.

nodes.label: Stale Closure Bug
nodes.rationale: A callback that closes over state but omits it from its dependency array always reads the initial value; the same callback written with a direct state reference must be recreated on every state change, causing unnecessary child re-renders.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: When the React Compiler is enabled it automatically optimizes re-renders, so manual memoization with memo()/useMemo() and manual dependency tracking become unnecessary.

nodes.label: Use Functional setState Updates
nodes.rationale: The functional update form of setState always operates on the latest state value, so callbacks need no state dependency. This eliminates stale closures, keeps callback references stable (children do not re-render), simplifies dependency arrays and prevents the most common React closure bugs.

nodes.label: Extract to Memoized Components
nodes.rationale: Extracting expensive work into a memoized child component lets the parent return early (e.g. a loading skeleton) before the expensive computation runs. Manual memo()/useMemo() is unnecessary when the React Compiler is enabled.

nodes.label: Extract Default Non-primitive Parameter Value from Memoized Component to Constant
nodes.norm_label: extract default non-primitive parameter value from memoized component to constant
nodes.rationale: A default array/function/object created inline inside a memoized component is a new instance on every rerender and fails the strict equality comparison used by memo(), breaking memoization. Hoisting the default to a module-level constant restores it.

nodes.label: Don't Define Components Inside Components
nodes.rationale: A component defined inside another component creates a new component type on every render, so React unmounts and remounts it, destroying internal state, re-running effects and recreating DOM nodes. Pass props instead of closing over parent variables.

nodes.label: Do Not Wrap a Simple Expression With a Primitive Result Type in useMemo
nodes.norm_label: do not wrap a simple expression with a primitive result type in usememo
nodes.rationale: Calling useMemo and comparing its dependency array costs more resources than evaluating a simple expression whose result is a primitive, so the memo wrapper is pure overhead.

nodes.label: Split Combined Hook Computations
nodes.rationale: A combined hook recomputes all of its tasks whenever any single dependency changes, even for tasks that do not use that value. Splitting independent tasks into separate hooks confines each recomputation to its own dependencies.

nodes.label: Use Activity Component for Show/Hide
nodes.rationale: Expensive components that frequently toggle visibility should keep their state and DOM; Activity hides without unmounting, avoiding expensive re-renders and state loss.

nodes.label: Animate SVG Wrapper Instead of SVG Element
nodes.norm_label: animate svg wrapper instead of svg element
nodes.rationale: Many browsers do not hardware-accelerate CSS3 animations applied to SVG elements; wrapping the SVG in a div and animating the wrapper allows GPU acceleration for transforms, opacity, translate, scale and rotate.

nodes.label: Use Explicit Conditional Rendering
nodes.rationale: The && operator renders falsy-but-renderable values such as 0 or NaN into the DOM, so an explicit ternary is used whenever the condition can be a falsy number.

nodes.label: Optimize SVG Precision
nodes.rationale: Reducing SVG coordinate precision decreases file size; the optimal precision depends on the viewBox size, so a reduction such as one decimal place is a general default.

nodes.label: Expo Development Client
nodes.rationale: Expo Go cannot load custom native modules, so a development client is required whenever the app needs native code that Expo Go does not bundle.

nodes.label: One Icon Family Per Platform
nodes.rationale: Mixing icon families or reusing SF names on Android produces an incoherent, partly blank icon set, so exactly one family is used per platform.

nodes.label: Material Icons Fallback
nodes.rationale: SF Symbols are an Apple asset that never render on Android, so an app shipping SF-only iconography ships blank icons and every icon needs a Material counterpart.

nodes.label: WebGPU Custom Build Requirement
nodes.rationale: WebGPU needs native GPU capabilities that Expo Go does not bundle, so it always requires a prebuild and a custom dev or production build.

nodes.label: Custom Build Requirements
nodes.rationale: Custom native builds are reserved for local Expo modules, Apple targets, third-party native modules and native configuration that cannot be expressed in app.json.

nodes.label: Expo Go First Strategy
nodes.rationale: Custom builds add complexity, slow iteration and require Xcode or Android Studio setup, so Expo Go is tried first and custom builds are created only when a feature truly demands native code.

nodes.label: Platform Design Language Adherence
nodes.rationale: Each platform keeps its own design language (Apple HIG on iOS, Material 3 on Android) so the app never dresses one platform in the other platform's uniform.

nodes.label: Semantic Color API
nodes.rationale: The expo-router Color wrapper over PlatformColor resolves platform-native colors on device and auto-adapts to light/dark and accessibility settings, eliminating separate light/dark hex tables.

nodes.label: Expo Go New Architecture Only
nodes.rationale: Expo Go only supports the New Architecture as of SDK 53, so apps on the legacy bridge must move to development builds.

nodes.label: allowBuilds: unrs-resolver
nodes.rationale: pnpm blocks dependency install scripts by default, so unrs-resolver is explicitly allow-listed: without it the resolver's native binary is never built and module resolution fails at build time.

nodes.label: Cache Storage API Calls
nodes.rationale: localStorage, sessionStorage and document.cookie are synchronous and expensive, so reading them on every call multiplies costly I/O. Cache reads in memory instead.

nodes.label: Cache Invalidation on External Storage Change
nodes.norm_label: cache invalidation on external storage change
nodes.rationale: If storage can change externally (another tab, server-set cookies) the in-memory cache becomes stale, so it must be invalidated on the 'storage' event and on visibilitychange.

nodes.label: Map-Based Storage Cache
nodes.rationale: A module-level Map is used instead of a hook so the cache works everywhere: utilities and event handlers, not just React components.

nodes.label: Hoist RegExp Creation
nodes.rationale: Creating a RegExp inside render recreates it on every render; hoisting to module scope or memoizing with useMemo avoids that recreation.

nodes.label: Global RegExp Mutable lastIndex State
nodes.rationale: Global regexes (/g) carry mutable lastIndex state, so repeated .test() calls on the same instance alternate results; this is a hazard when hoisting a shared regex.

nodes.label: Hoist Static JSX Elements
nodes.rationale: Extracting static JSX outside the component reuses the same element instead of recreating it on every render, which matters most for large static SVG nodes.

nodes.label: Static SVG Node Reuse
nodes.rationale: Large and static SVG nodes are expensive to recreate on every render, so hoisting them yields the biggest benefit of the pattern.

nodes.label: Defer State Reads to Usage Point
nodes.norm_label: defer state reads to usage point
nodes.rationale: Subscribing to dynamic state such as searchParams or localStorage when the value is only read inside a callback causes needless re-renders; reading on demand avoids the subscription entirely.

nodes.label: Next.js fetch request memoization
nodes.rationale: Next.js extends fetch with automatic request memoization, so identical URLs and options are already deduplicated within a request and do not need React.cache().

nodes.label: React.cache()
nodes.rationale: React.cache() deduplicates calls only within the scope of a single request; its scope limitation is what motivates cross-request LRU caching.

nodes.label: Module Scope as Process-Wide Shared Memory
nodes.norm_label: module scope as process-wide shared memory
nodes.rationale: On the server, module scope is shared by all concurrent requests in the process, so it is only safe for immutable static assets, correctly keyed cross-request caches, and singletons that hold no request- or user-specific mutable data.

nodes.label: Cross-Request LRU Caching
nodes.rationale: React.cache() only deduplicates within a single request, so sequential user actions that need the same data across requests require a cross-request LRU cache. Vercel Fluid Compute shares one function instance across concurrent requests so the cache persists without Redis; traditional serverless needs an external cache.

nodes.label: Per-Request Deduplication with React.cache()
nodes.rationale: React.cache() memoizes by shallow (Object.is) equality within a request, so inline object arguments always miss the cache. It is essential for database queries, heavy computations, authentication checks and file system operations that are not covered by the automatic fetch request memoization in Next.js.

nodes.label: Hoist Static I/O to Module Level
nodes.norm_label: hoist static i/o to module level
nodes.rationale: Module-level code runs once when the module is first imported, so hoisting static asset reads (fonts for OG images, logos, config files, email templates) removes repeated filesystem or network I/O on every request. Assets that vary per request, change at runtime, are too large or are sensitive must not be hoisted.

nodes.label: Avoid Shared Module State for Request Data
nodes.norm_label: avoid shared module state for request data
nodes.rationale: Server renders run concurrently in the same process, so mutable module-level variables used for request-scoped data cause race conditions, cross-request contamination and leaks of one user's data into another user's response. Module scope on the server must be treated as process-wide shared memory, not request-local state.

nodes.label: Automatic Memoization
nodes.rationale: React Compiler memoizes components and values at build time, which removes the need for manual useMemo, useCallback and React.memo.

nodes.label: Continuous Native Generation
nodes.rationale: When neither ios/ nor android/ exists the project uses Continuous Native Generation and regenerates native projects at build time, so prebuild and cache-clearing steps are skipped.

nodes.label: Hermes V1 Memory Regression
nodes.rationale: SDK 55 with Hermes V1, SDK 56 and older SDK 57 releases contain a Hermes V1 memory regression when importing react-native-worklets or reanimated, so the guide skips SDK 56 and jumps straight to SDK 57.

nodes.label: Bundle Size Optimization
nodes.rationale: Reducing initial bundle size improves Time to Interactive and Largest Contentful Paint.

nodes.label: Next.js Output File Tracing
nodes.rationale: Next.js statically analyzes import, require and fs usage to trace output files, so path.join(process.cwd(), someVar) widens the traced set even for a two-value enum.

nodes.label: typeof window !== 'undefined' SSR guard
nodes.rationale: Client-only check placed around a dynamic import so the module is not bundled for SSR, optimizing server bundle size and build speed.

nodes.label: Dynamic import() code splitting
nodes.rationale: import() splits a module into its own chunk that is fetched on demand instead of being pulled into the initial module graph.

nodes.label: next/dynamic
nodes.rationale: Component-level lazy loading API; with { ssr: false } the underlying module is fetched only on the client when the component actually renders.

nodes.label: Next.js output file tracing documentation
nodes.rationale: Documents how Next.js traces output files at build time and why dynamic path composition widens the traced set.

nodes.label: Prefer Statically Analyzable Paths
nodes.rationale: Hiding real paths behind variables forces bundlers to include a broad set of candidate files or widen file tracing, which inflates server bundles, slows builds, worsens cold starts and increases memory use; explicit maps and literal paths keep the reachable set narrow and predictable.

nodes.label: Conditional Module Loading
nodes.rationale: Large data or module payloads should only load when the feature that needs them is activated, and the typeof window guard keeps them out of the SSR bundle, improving server bundle size and build speed.

nodes.label: Defer Non-Critical Third-Party Libraries
nodes.rationale: Analytics, logging and error tracking do not block user interaction, so loading them after hydration removes them from the critical bundle without hurting UX.

nodes.label: Dynamic Imports for Heavy Components
nodes.rationale: Lazy-loading large components that are not needed on the first render keeps them out of the main chunk, directly improving TTI and LCP (Monaco alone is ~300KB of main bundle).

nodes.label: Preload Based on User Intent
nodes.rationale: Pre-warming a heavy bundle on hover/focus or once a feature flag is enabled removes perceived latency while keeping the module out of the initial bundle; the typeof window check keeps preloaded modules out of the server bundle.

nodes.label: Eliminating Waterfalls
nodes.rationale: Waterfalls are the #1 performance killer because each sequential await adds full network latency; eliminating them yields the largest gains.

nodes.label: better-all (dependency-aware parallelization library)
nodes.rationale: Starts each task at the earliest moment its dependencies allow, maximizing parallelism without manually chaining promises.

nodes.label: Promise.all()
nodes.rationale: Awaits an array of promises concurrently and resolves once all settle; it is the core primitive for removing request waterfalls when operations have no interdependencies.

nodes.label: React Suspense boundary
nodes.rationale: Lets a slow child suspend while the surrounding layout renders immediately, showing a fallback until the child's data resolves.

nodes.label: use() (React promise unwrapping)
nodes.rationale: Unwraps a promise during render so several components can share one in-flight request instead of each triggering its own fetch.

nodes.label: Rule Document Template
nodes.rationale: Every rule file follows this shape - YAML frontmatter (title, impact, impactDescription, tags) plus Incorrect/Correct code blocks - so agents can pattern-match violations and generate the refactor automatically.

nodes.label: Prevent Waterfall Chains in API Routes
nodes.norm_label: prevent waterfall chains in api routes
nodes.rationale: Sequential awaits in route handlers and Server Actions serialize full network latency; starting independent operations immediately and awaiting them together removes the chain (2-10x improvement).

nodes.label: Check Cheap Conditions Before Async Flags
nodes.norm_label: check cheap conditions before async flags
nodes.rationale: When a compound condition mixes an awaited flag with a cheap synchronous guard, evaluating the cheap condition first avoids paying for a network, feature-flag, React.cache or DB call on a path that can never be taken; the original order should be kept when the cheap condition is expensive or depends on the flag.

nodes.label: Defer Await Until Needed
nodes.rationale: Moving an await into the branch that consumes its result keeps unneeded code paths from blocking; the reordering is most valuable when the skipped branch is frequently taken or the deferred operation is expensive.

nodes.label: Dependency-Based Parallelization
nodes.rationale: With partial dependencies a generic Promise.all still leaves work waiting on unrelated siblings; a dependency-aware runner starts each task at the earliest possible moment (2-10x improvement).

nodes.label: Promise.all() for Independent Operations
nodes.rationale: Awaiting independent operations one after another costs one network round trip each; awaiting them together collapses three round trips into one.

nodes.label: Strategic Suspense Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Awaiting data in an async component blocks the whole layout; moving the await behind a Suspense boundary paints the wrapper immediately and streams the data in, trading faster initial paint against possible layout shift. Not appropriate for SEO-critical content, layout-critical data, tiny fast queries, or when layout shift must be avoided.

nodes.rationale: Content questions must be answered honestly to get an appropriate age rating, using the NONE / INFREQUENT_OR_MILD / FREQUENT_OR_INTENSE descriptors plus boolean flags such as gambling, unrestrictedWebAccess and seventeenPlus.

nodes.rationale: JavaScript configuration allows dynamic values such as a copyright year, fetched translations from a CMS, or environment-specific promo text; eas.json points cli.metadataPath at store.config.js. Note that eas metadata:pull creates a JSON file, so it does not update a JS config automatically.

nodes.label: App Store Localization
nodes.rationale: Metadata is localized per target market with a fixed set of supported locales, and keywords should be researched per locale because direct translations often miss regional search terms.

nodes.label: App Store Optimization (ASO)
nodes.rationale: The title is the most important ranking factor, so the brand name plus one or two strongest keywords go first; the subtitle carries the value proposition without duplicating title words, and the 100-character keyword field uses every character with no spaces after commas.

nodes.label: App Store Release Strategy
nodes.rationale: automaticRelease controls whether release happens on approval, manually, or at an RFC 3339 date, and phasedRelease gives a 7-day gradual rollout (1%, 2%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%, 100%) so a bad release can be caught early.

nodes.label: App Review Information
nodes.rationale: The review block provides contact info and demo credentials so the App Review team can actually exercise login-gated features; missing demo accounts are a listed rejection reason.

nodes.label: EAS Metadata and store.config.json
nodes.rationale: EAS Metadata automates App Store presence management from the command line using a store.config.json file instead of manually filling forms in App Store Connect, and includes built-in validation to catch common rejection pitfalls. Current status: Preview, Apple App Store only.

nodes.label: App Review Process and Rejection Reasons
nodes.norm_label: app review process and rejection reasons
nodes.rationale: Reviewers check functionality, UI/UX against the Human Interface Guidelines, content, privacy and legal compliance; common rejections include crashes, incomplete metadata, placeholder content, missing login credentials, a missing privacy policy and Guideline 4.2 minimum functionality.

nodes.label: App Store Connect First-Time Setup
nodes.rationale: The app record must exist in App Store Connect before submission, with bundle ID matching the archive, plus pricing/availability, app privacy declarations and reviewer contact information; Xcode is authoritative for the bundle ID of checked-in native projects.

nodes.label: Distribution Certificates and Provisioning Profiles
nodes.rationale: A distribution certificate is limited to three per Apple Developer account and valid for one year, while App Store provisioning profiles link app, certificate and entitlements without device UDIDs; EAS manages both automatically.

nodes.label: Complete the Public Release Procedure
nodes.rationale: EAS Submit only uploads the binary; public distribution continues in App Store Connect by selecting the exact processed build, completing listing and review information, adding for review then submitting for review, and applying the chosen release timing. Uploading a TestFlight beta does not itself request a public launch.

nodes.label: iOS Release Options
nodes.rationale: Automatic, scheduled and phased release are fragments of store.config.json for EAS Metadata, but uploading with EAS Submit still requires selecting the processed build and completing App Review before a public release.

nodes.label: TestFlight versus App Store Distribution
nodes.rationale: TestFlight covers beta testing (up to 100 internal and 10,000 external testers, builds expiring after 90 days, external beta review required) while a public App Store release additionally requires passing App Review.
